# OzzyRockerPL — scoring system

- Original source: [OzzyRockerPL — scoring system](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2829972690)
- Author / publication: OzzyRockerPL / Steam Community
- Language / date: English; published and updated 2022-07-09
- Access: Full guide page retrieved directly
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09
- Archived copy: none found in the Wayback Machine (checked 2026-09-09)
- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes and both tables (no redistribution grant on Steam guides, so not transcribed)

Reported mission-end points:

| Event | Points |
| --- | ---: |
| Main mission completed | 1,000 |
| Ambush shield obtained | 1,000 |
| Ground/coffer money, per £100 | 10 |
| Soldier killed | 50 |
| Soldier still unconscious or bound at completion | 70 |
| Royal collectible | 1,000 |
| Guy or the Sheriff defeated | 100 |

The author reports no points for elapsed time, looted personal money, pre-existing corpses, recovered prisoners, netted/trapped enemies, or the Silver Arrow. Allied kills count.

Includes seventeen mission discussions, conditional Free Lincoln, and a score table. It warns about two swordsmen breaking The Letter's conversation. Pre-existing corpses reportedly affect spared lives despite awarding no points.

**Limitations:** community findings; maxima, rounding, and event classification are unverified.

## Detailed notes

Guide metadata at retrieval: v1.0, posted 9 Jul 2022 1:37am and updated 1:50am the same day; categories Achievements, Gameplay Basics, Maps or Levels, Secrets, Walkthroughs; 644 unique visitors, 4 favourites, 2 comments. Sections: Introduction, Points, Overview, Table with maximum scores, Links.

**Introduction.** Mission-end score is shown but never explained in game; most players watch only the spared-lives ratio. The author invites corrections and better scores.

**Points** (the table in the summary above is the complete list). Additional statements: quest completion points apply only to the 17 main missions; shields count only in Sherwood ambushes; personal money is ignored probably to stop purse-throw exploits; knocked-out or tied soldiers count only if still restrained at mission end; soldiers dead before the mission starts (Pillaging, The Black Castle, The March on York) give nothing; enemies in Stuteley's net or in ambush traps (nets, pits) give nothing; the Silver Arrow is a tournament prize, not a royal item; losing Merry Men or allied soldiers costs nothing; kills by allied soldiers do count.

**Per-mission notes.**
1. Finding Godwin: Robin alone, so nobody can be tied; on Hard soldiers wake quickly, but recovery time depends on remaining health, so weaken them, retreat, return and punch; some soldiers change position or behaviour after the first encounter; Robin can leave and re-enter the castle over the east wall, which enemies cannot climb.
2. Rescuing Stuteley: the inner-castle gate stays closed. Show yourself to a pro-sheriff civilian so they alarm the officer through the north tower; after things calm down a crossbowman relocates above the gate where Robin can shoot him. Suggested order: shoot the officer near the gate, then the second crossbowman when he comes into bow range, wait, then throw a purse at the four "lancers" (the manual's term; the author calls them recruits) and shoot the winner. Knights are immune to arrows but can be engaged in melee through the gate bars; the author judges that not worth the reloads.
3. Scarlet Night: nothing special.
4. Confessions of an Outlaw: seven bodyguards at the party in the sheriff's chamber cannot be attacked.
5. The Prince and the Outlaw: twelve soldiers cannot be attacked (per the summary's soldier count).
6. Pillaging: seven pre-placed corpses give no points but count against the spared ratio.
7. The Evening Visitor: the five soldiers in the western tower belong to the sheriff, not Ranulph, so killing them does not fail the mission; knocking out scores more anyway.
8. The Godfather in Prison: two crossbowmen and a halberdier near Guy of Gisbourne can be shot with Quick Actions.
9. The Lock-up and the Friar: one unreachable soldier.
10. The Silver Arrow: five unreachable soldiers.
11. A Wedding and a Funeral: three unreachable, including one in the far north-east.
12. The Escape: nothing special.
13. The Letter: do not attack the two swordsmen near a tower in the citadel (they can be lured out, for example by whistling); doing so breaks the game after the villains' conversation. Plus one unreachable soldier in the far north-east.
14. Free Lincoln: only offered if Lincoln is lost.
15. The Black Castle: twenty-one pre-placed corpses (no points, count against ratio); one unreachable soldier.
16. The March on York: six pre-placed corpses; one unreachable soldier in the far north-east.
17. Last Challenge: a swordsman becomes an ally if you talk to a beggar and then a man in the church vestry; to score him, confront him before talking about him. Four other soldiers unreachable.

**Comments.** Asked whether all coffers in Rescuing Stuteley can be collected, the author (23 May 2023) lists £100 in the church vestry, £500 near the tax collector in the south and £500 on a roof in the north; the last appears after reading the scroll obtained by paying the beggar at least six times.
